annotation_description: The player mulliganed a 7-card hand that had 2 Plains, multiple white creatures on a reasonable curve (Infantry Veteran at 1, Daybreak Charger at 2, Knight of the Tusk at 6), a combat trick (Moment of Triumph), and a powerful enchantment (Blessed Sanctuary). While the hand only has 2 lands and no non-white mana sources, the white creatures form a functional curve. With 2 lands and draws to find more, this hand is keepable - especially since mulliganing to 6 means losing a card and potentially getting a worse hand.

Playing Forest turn 1 instead of Treetop Village wastes the opportunity to get the 'enters tapped' downside out of the way on a turn with no 1-drops to cast. This delays Uktabi Orangutan by a full turn: with Treetop Village T1, the line is T2 Swamp→Oathsworn Vampire, T3 Forest→Uktabi Orangutan. With Forest T1, the line becomes T2 Swamp→Vampire, T3 Treetop Village (tapped, can't cast 3-drop), T4 Forest→Orangutan.
human_notes: treetop village strictly better than forest here (unless you're worried about wasteland or something)

annotation_description: Playing Forest instead of Swamp wastes the opportunity to cast Oathsworn Vampire this turn. With Forest + Swamp, the player has exactly {1}{B} to cast the 2/2 vampire. Playing a second Forest leaves 2 green mana with nothing castable.
human_notes: better to play swamp so you can get the oathsworn vampire down
better to play orangutan later when you can get etb value. if cub attacks you probably won't block it anyways, so etb tapped is fine
